traced_causes.finding: publishHeartbeat returned status "unconfigured" and made zero requests when no admin credential was present, so a cycle that ran every due job still left ops:scheduler:heartbeat absent and exited without publishing anything.
traced_causes.trigger_condition: The launchd job definition declared no environment, and a launchd agent inherits no login shell, so the credential never reached the runner.
traced_causes.evidence: Reproduced directly: publishHeartbeat with no credential returned {"status":"unconfigured"} with 0 HTTP calls.
traced_causes.repair: An unpublishable heartbeat is a failed cycle with a named reason, persisted to the state directory; the job definition names the state directory, the heartbeat route, and a mode-0600 credential file.

traced_causes.finding: The stored heartbeat carried only observed_at, run_key, pending_outbox and due_jobs, so no receipt could be matched to the run that wrote it and any caller could assert liveness.
traced_causes.repair: workflow, run_id, source_revision and result are required; an incomplete or generic heartbeat is rejected with 400 and never stored, and the runner verifies its own run identity round-tripped rather than trusting the endpoint's overall ok.

traced_causes.finding: The scheduler watchdog called the alert relay with no workflow_run_url and no receipt_url, so the human-grade paragraph rendered "Workflow run: null. Raw receipt: null." The same relay already rejected external callers that omitted those links.
traced_causes.evidence: Reproduced on the unrepaired path: "scheduler-heartbeat broke: scheduler heartbeat missing. ... Workflow run: null. Raw receipt: null."
traced_causes.repair: Scheduler and served-artifact guards must supply workflow, source revision, a validated run link and a validated raw-receipt link. Missing evidence holds the alert and records a delivery finding; the endpoint still fails closed with 503.

traced_causes.finding: The check rebuilt main and compared artifact hashes against the served artifact. The production deploy builds with refreshed decision outcomes drawn from live sources, so a rebuild of the same revision cannot reproduce the deployed bytes and the hash comparison could never pass.
traced_causes.evidence: Workflow run 33574860994 reported exactly one finding, "artifact hash mismatch", with live_source_commit_sha dd4b708b6fe39bf8b2ea635ef3d4f493c4751ace, which was main's own tip; the rebuild produced 2ddd2888fde7f715b6029942c26caa4edc46db1ee12bdaa4a6a6bc850511153a against the served 21fa43eba688d2095629ec55b70c0d59d11521c751d6d6a33a9e7ece960675e8. Every scheduled run of this workflow in the retained history failed the same way across many different revisions.
traced_causes.repair: The comparison basis is the manifest the last successful production deploy published. Deploy lag is a separate finding naming both revisions, so an artifact matching an older deploy is still nonzero and carries its own signature.

hypotheses_tested.hypothesis: The dead scheduler is responsible for regenerating and deploying the served artifact, so one broken scheduler explains both alarms.
hypotheses_tested.basis: The scheduled jobs are action-links, source-contracts, source-freshness and digest-shadow; none regenerates or deploys the served artifact. The served artifact is published by the production deploy on push to main. The two failures share no cause and keep separate signatures.

hypotheses_tested.hypothesis: The served artifact lagged main after a high-merge day.
hypotheses_tested.verdict: not supported by the run's own evidence
hypotheses_tested.basis: The run recorded the served artifact at main's own revision and raised no source-commit finding. The mismatch was between two builds of the same revision, not between two revisions.

register_discrepancy.observed_gap: The scheduler-heartbeat item was folded into that record, but no scheduled cycle ever wrote a heartbeat and the watchdog's own alerts carried null run and receipt evidence. The completed record is left unamended; this receipt is the discrepancy note.
